note: Shared Reroute advisory (ADVZY) reference cases, taken from the vATCSCC TMI material cited by VATUSA/OIS#437. The renderer is backend/src/advisory.rs (render_reroute); this file is what its tests assert against, so an example is written once and the document format cannot quietly drift. Every field is written out, null where absent, so a case reads as a complete advisory. The backend is authoritative: if a case and an implementation disagree, the backend decides which is wrong. One deliberate deviation from the source document is recorded per case in `deviation`.

cases.name: advzy-004-single-segment
cases.why: The reference single-segment reroute, every field populated. Every section is load-bearing: drop a label, the TMI ID, the valid window or the signature and this fails.

cases.name: advzy-005-multi-segment
cases.why: The reference multi-segment reroute: two tables (origin segments, then destination segments), an ETD-based valid period, and the remarks/associated-restrictions/modifications lines carrying text rather than being bare.
cases.deviation: The source document wraps a long route onto a continuation line indented to the ROUTE column, but not by any stated rule - measured inline widths are LAS 62 (not wrapped), SEA 50 (not wrapped), LAX 65 (wrapped), SFO 65 (wrapped), so the threshold is a column artifact of the source PDF rather than a spec. Each route therefore renders on one line here. If a real wrap width is ever documented, this case is where it gets pinned.
